DOW-UAP-D098, Film Analysis of Unidentified Objects, 1953
DOW-UAP-D098、未確認物体のフィルム分析、1953 年
Department of War
米国戦争省
8/7/26
2026年8月7日（Release 05）
1950, 1952
Montana, Utah
モンタナ州、ユタ州
PDF
PDF
This file contains a memorandum relating to the U.S. Naval Photographic Interpretation Center’s assessment of two films allegedly depicting unidentified airborne objects, captured in Montana and Utah in 1950 and 1952, respectively. The file documents the Center’s analytic process, assumptions that constrained its confidence level, tentative conclusions, and recommendations for future research. The Center assessed, generally, that the objects depicted in the film demonstrated characteristics that were inconsistent with those of natural phenomena or commonly known aerospace technologies. The memorandum documents the Center’s recommendation for a more well-resourced investigation to corroborate its presumptive findings, citing a lack of funding and personnel. The accompanying charts compare the film’s luminosity with the apparent angular size of the phenomena, using contemporary mathematical modeling and photogrammetric analysis techniques.
このファイルには、1950年と1952年にそれぞれモンタナ州とユタ州で撮影された、未確認の空中物体を描いたとされる2本の映画に対する米国海軍写真通訳センターの評価に関する覚書が含まれている。このファイルには、センターの分析プロセス、信頼レベルを制約する仮定、暫定的な結論、将来の研究への推奨事項が記録されています。同センターは、一般的に、映画に描かれた物体は、自然現象や一般に知られている航空宇宙技術の特徴と矛盾する特徴を示していると評価した。この覚書には、資金と人員の不足を理由に、推定の調査結果を裏付けるために、より十分な資源を投入した調査を行うようセンターが勧告したことが文書化されている。添付のチャートは、現代の数学モデリングと写真測量分析技術を使用して、フィルムの明るさと現象の見かけの角度サイズを比較しています。
既に公開済み

機関: U.S. Naval Photographic Interpretation Center から海軍情報部宛の機密進捗報告（1953年）で、1952年7月2日ユタ州撮影の16mmカラー映画（約30フィート）および1950年モンタナ撮影分の解析について記載。解析手法としてはフィルム複写・色補正、ストップフレーム投影でのプロット作成、Densichronによる輝度（密度）測定、相対サイズ測定などを実施。ユタ映像は劣化が著しく複写を使用。フィルムは3部に区分（Part I f/8、Part II f/16 パン、Part III f/16 固定）し、青白色の光源が3群にわたって観察された。輝度と映像上のサイズは相関し、解析者の多数意見はこれらが発光体（light sources）であるとする一方、反射面（高反射体）や既知の気象・動物・航空機・気球では説明できないと結論付けた。速度・加速度は（解析上の仮定に基づき）非常に大きく算出され、例としてPart IIIの測定から速度範囲の参考値が示され（最大・最小の例示）、加速度は数十～数百gのオーダーとして極めて高い値となった。モンタナ映像では地上物体を対照として用い、速度・加速度算定はより信頼性があるとされた。推定サイズは観測者からの距離を5マイルと仮定した場合で16～98フィート。解析には機材・資金・人員の制約やフィルムが複写の複写である等の限界があり、追加試験（参照文献に基づく分光測定等）が提案されている。文書は機密扱い。
Source: Confidential progress report from the U.S. Naval Photographic Interpretation Center to the Director of Naval Intelligence (1953) on interpretation of 16mm color motion-picture films of unidentified objects (Utah, 2 July 1952; Montana, 1950). Methods included film duplication and color correction, stop-frame projection for overlay plotting, densitometry with a Densichron instrument, and relative-size measurements. The Utah film was in poor condition and analyzed in three segments (Part I: f/8; Part II: f/16 with panning; Part III: f/16 steady). Three distinct groups of blue-white lights were observed; brightness correlated with apparent size. Analysts judged the images most likely to be light sources rather than simple reflections, and concluded they could not be identified as known natural phenomena, aircraft, birds, or balloons. Velocity and acceleration computations (made under stated assumptions, e.g. assumed range) yielded very large values; example measurements from Utah Part III produced high speed estimates and accelerations on the order of tens to hundreds of g. Montana measurements, using terrestrial objects as controls, were considered more reliable and also indicated high speeds/accelerations. Size estimates assuming a 5-mile range were about 16–98 feet. The report cites limitations (film condition, duplicate copy, equipment/funding/personnel constraints) and recommends further tests, including spectrophotometric analysis. The material is classified confidential.

CIA-UAP-D022, Unidentified Flying Object Reported near Puerto Rico, 1965
CIA-UAP-D022、プエルトリコ近郊で報告された未確認飛行物体、1965年
CIA
CIA
8/7/26
2026年8月7日（Release 05）

Caribbean Sea
カリブ海
PDF
PDF
This file contains Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) memoranda exchanged between the Assistant Director for Special Activities (AD/SA) and the Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence (AD/SI) regarding an incident allegedly involving unidentified aircraft in the vicinity of Puerto Rico. The AD/SI was then-responsible for analyzing foreign scientific advancements and technological threats, such as Soviet nuclear, chemical, and ballistic missile capabilities. The AD/SA managed the CIA’s classified overhead reconnaissance operations, including the deployment of advanced aircraft like the U-2 and A-12 OXCART. Together, these offices ensured the United States could both gather critical intelligence over contested territories and accurately evaluate the technical capabilities of foreign adversaries during the Cold War. The memoranda refer to an incident on November 19, 1964, in which a U.S. Naval aviator described observing an unidentified object as “delta-shaped, about the size of a jet fighter.” The pilot visually estimated the object’s velocity as Mach 3 (approximately 2,200 mph). A corresponding track from an AN/SPS-49 radar system aboard a U.S. Navy guided missile destroyer in the area, USS Gyatt, measured the object’s speed at 3,800 knots (approximately 4,373 mph). The memoranda indicate that, in the opinion of the AD/SI, the object was conceivably associated with foreign intelligence gathering activities, citing active missile testing within the AFWR, or Atlantic Fleet Weapons Range, as being an attractive reconnaissance target. The AD/SA and AD/SI also ruled out domestic experimental aircraft, such as the YF-12A OXCART, as a potential attribution.
このファイルには、プエルトリコ近郊で未確認航空機が関与したとされる事件に関して、特別活動担当次官補 (AD/SA) と科学情報担当次官補 (AD/SI) の間で交わされた中央情報局 (CIA) の覚書が含まれています。当時、AD/SI は外国の科学の進歩とソ連の核、化学、弾道ミサイル能力などの技術的脅威の分析を担当していました。 AD/SA は、U-2 や A-12 OXCART などの最新鋭航空機の配備を含む、CIA の機密上空偵察活動を管理しました。これらの事務所により、米国は冷戦中に紛争地域に関する重要な情報を収集し、外国の敵の技術的能力を正確に評価できるようになった。この覚書は、1964年11月19日の事件に言及しており、この事件では、米海軍飛行士が未確認物体を観察した際に「ジェット戦闘機ほどの大きさのデルタ型」であると述べた。パイロットは物体の速度を視覚的にマッハ 3 (時速約 2,200 マイル) と推定しました。この海域の米海軍誘導ミサイル駆逐艦USSギャットに搭載されたAN/SPS-49レーダーシステムからの対応する追跡では、物体の速度が3,800ノット（時速約4,373マイル）であることが測定された。覚書は、AD/SIの見解では、この物体はおそらく外国の情報収集活動に関連しており、AFWR（大西洋艦隊兵器射程）内での活発なミサイル実験が魅力的な偵察目標であると言及していることを示している。 AD/SA と AD/SI はまた、YF-12A OXCART などの国産実験機を潜在的な帰属として除外しました。

機密指定（TOP SECRET、BYEMAN、OXCART）文書（1 FEB 1965）。差出人はACK C. L.（大佐、Assistant Director (Special Activities)）で、宛先は科学情報担当アシスタントディレクター。内容は、1964年11月18–24日頃のプエルトリコ付近での未確認飛行物体（UFO）に関する情報についてで、OSIおよびOSAが同様の情報を受領したと記載されている。カリブ海方面司令官からの電報でCO RameyがUFOをYF-12Aと識別した旨が伝えられたが、ONIは本件がYF-12Aや同種のロッキード機ではないと結論付けたと報告している。海軍から関連通信と原始レーダーフィルム（添付1）およびプリントが提供されており、OSI（場合によってはOELと共同で）に対し、これらのレーダー写真を科学的に評価して追加情報が得られるかを調査するよう要請している。調査完了後、資料はTCO/BCO/OSA経由で海軍に返却するよう求めている。文書には米国スパイ法（18 U.S.C. §§793,794）に基づく取扱警告が付されている。
Top-secret BYEMAN/OXCART memorandum dated 1 Feb 1965 from ACK C. L. (Colonel, Assistant Director, Special Activities) to the Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence. It reports that OSI and OSA received similar reports of a UFO near Puerto Rico during 18–24 November 1964. A cable from the Commander, Caribbean Sea Frontier to CINCLANTFLT stated CO Ramey had identified the object as a YF-12A; however, ONI, apparently influenced by the authors' efforts, concluded the object was not a YF-12A or similar Lockheed aircraft. The Navy provided related traffic and original radar film (Attachment 1) with prints. The memo requests OSI, possibly with OEL, to evaluate the radar photography scientifically to determine if further information regarding a high‑speed, high‑altitude UFO can be obtained, and requests return of the documents, film, and prints to TCO/BCO/OSA for return to the Navy upon completion. The document retains TOP SECRET handling markings and includes a statutory security warning (18 U.S.C. §§793, 794).

This document contains briefing material prepared for Mr. Walter N. Elder, Executive Assistant to the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), regarding a November 19, 1964, incident allegedly involving unidentified aircraft in the vicinity of Puerto Rico. The previous entry in this collection, CIA-UAP-D022, contains CIA memoranda on the same subject matter. The briefing includes additional details regarding that incident, including a characterization of the meteorological conditions and sensing capabilities of nearby U.S. military collection systems. The briefing states that a radar system aboard USS Gyatt, a guided missile destroyer operating in the vicinity, detected a contact tracking more than 3,800 knots (approximately 4,373 mph) over a period of 21 minutes. The briefing contains visual estimates regarding the phenomenon’s apparent capabilities from the pilot of an F-8 Crusader who was present during the incident.

On 19 November, a U.S. ship identified in the text as Wyatt picked up a fighter on radar; the same object appeared on Wyatt's radar and closed to within a few miles of the fighter. That night a Crusader pilot reportedly observed a delta-shaped object in full moonlight with good visibility. On 24 November, during operations at the Atlantic Fleet Weapons Range a high-speed, high-altitude target reportedly pulled away rapidly from another Crusader aircraft (the text records “Mach . 99, 45,000 feet”). The U.S.S. Gyatt (Gyatt in the text) confirmed tracking with motion pictures of the radar scope, and the pilot estimated speed in excess of Mach 3. The Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI) reported no further information and was requested to notify of similar incidents in the future. The document also notes the U.S.S. Gyatt is a Navy surface-to-… missile destroyer equipped with the latest, most accurate [equipment], but this portion is truncated.

This document is a U.S. Department of State diplomatic cable from the U.S. Embassy in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil to the Office of the Secretary of State in Washington, D.C., on November 14, 1963. This cable documents an effort by the Embassy to verify that the Department had assessed certain content published in a local newspaper as inauthentic, following a discussion on a poor-quality telephone connection the previous night. To ensure both offices were referencing the same reporting, the cable cites descriptive language paraphrased from the press, namely a “large metal manned balloon” and a “dead crewman aboard wearing [a] uniform or spacesuit with strange markings.” The cable concludes with the embassy’s understanding that an object assessed to be a weather balloon had been reported in the vicinity, but that no such object had been found to have crashed. A follow-on correspondence regarding the alleged incident is included in this collection under the title “DOS-UAP-D002.”
この文書は、1963 年 11 月 14 日に、ブラジルのリオデジャネイロにある米国大使館からワシントン D.C. の国務長官室に送信された米国国務省の外交公電です。この公電は、前夜の低品質の電話接続に関する議論を受けて、同省が地元の新聞に掲載された特定の内容を本物ではないと評価したことを確認するための大使館の取り組みを文書化したものです。両局が同じ報道を参照していることを確認するために、電報は報道機関からの言い換え、つまり「大きな金属製の有人気球」と「奇妙な模様が付いた制服や宇宙服を着た乗組員の死亡」を引用している。この公電は、気象気球と推定される物体が付近で報告されたが、そのような物体が墜落したことは発見されていないと大使館が理解していると結論づけている。疑惑の事件に関するその後の通信は、「DOS-UAP-D002」というタイトルでこのコレクションに含まれています。

This document is a U.S. Department of State diplomatic cable from the U.S. Embassy in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil to the Office of the Secretary of State in Washington, D.C., on November 20, 1963. This cable relays the findings of the scientific attaché at the American Consulate in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, that a widely reported incident allegedly involving a crashed unidentified object was unsubstantiated, characterizing the reports as a fabrication originating in Rio de Janeiro. The Consulate cites a lack of contemporary local reporting regarding the alleged incident, as well as contradictory reporting from local newspapers after the fact, as evidence that the published claims are unsubstantiated. The Consulate also cites a statement from the Brazilian Ministry of Aeronautics categorically denying that there was “any “strange object” in Conde [Bahia].” This correspondence follows a previous exchange between the Embassy and the Department of State, included in this collection under the title “DOS-UAP-D001.”

Department of State cable. Subject: "Negative Report on UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) Reportedly Sighted Near Salvador, Bahia on November 8, 1964." Information copies of the cited Embtel were sent to the Department with a request that they be passed to Defense (for the Air Force) and NASA. Consul Harold Midkiff replied by telegram No. 157 (November 14) stating the story of a strange object descending in the Conde region appeared fabricated in Rio; reporters and others who rushed to the area said no one saw such an object. The Secretary of Public Security speculated it might have been a weather balloon, but no sighting was verified. Midkiff also forwarded two local newspaper clippings (Diario de Noticias, Nov. 9; Jornal da Bahia, Nov. 11) reporting that the Ministry of Aeronautics denied any strange object in Conde and that the Jornal da Bahia piece was titled "The Airship that wasn't there." The document is declassified NND 939551.

DOW-UAP-D099、「幽霊ロケット」事件の情報調査、1947年

This document is a U.S. Department of War General Staff intelligence review assessing incidents involving unidentified “Ghost Rockets” reported over Sweden and other Scandinavian countries beginning in May 1946. The review includes an analysis of observational reports, statements from the Swedish government, and reporting from the U.S. military attaché in Stockholm. The review highlights the inconclusive nature of the contemporary evidence available to substantiate reports from civilian and military observers. The review also documents a change in the public stance of the Swedish Defense Staff, which privately attributed the objects to Soviet V-1 missile tests launched from Peenemünde. Peenemünde is a then-occupied municipality in northeastern Germany that had been associated with the development of the V-1 and V-2 rocket program during World War II. The Swedish assessment publicly shifted from an unknown technological origin to one of a “celestial origin.” The review suggests that this shift was a deliberate effort to avoid diplomatic conflict with the Soviet Union. The report’s final assessment concludes that while most reported incidents were likely misidentified natural phenomena, the “best evidence” suggested a small number of “real incidents” involving low-flying V-1 type missiles, likely attributable to Soviet tests of captured German technology.
この文書は、1946年5月からスウェーデンおよび他のスカンジナビア諸国で報告された未確認の「幽霊ロケット弾」に関する事件を評価する米国陸軍参謀本部情報調査である。この調査には、観測報告、スウェーデン政府の声明、およびストックホルムの米陸軍武官からの報告の分析が含まれている。この調査は、民間および軍の監視員からの報告を実証するために利用できる現代の証拠が決定的ではない性質を強調している。この調査はまた、物体はペーネミュンデから発射されたソ連のV-1ミサイル実験によるものであると非公式に主張していたスウェーデン国防参謀の公的立場の変化も記録している。ペーネミュンデはドイツ北東部にある当時占領下の自治体で、第二次世界大戦中に V-1 および V-2 ロケット計画の開発に関与していました。スウェーデンの評価は、未知の技術的起源から「天体の起源」の1つに公的に変更されました。この検討は、この変更がソ連との外交摩擦を避けるための意図的な努力であったことを示唆している。報告書の最終評価では、報告された事件のほとんどは誤認された自然現象である可能性が高いが、「最良の証拠」は、低空飛行のV-1型ミサイルが関与した少数の「実際の事件」を示唆しており、おそらく鹵獲したドイツ技術のソ連による実験に起因すると結論付けている。
既に公開済み
documents.summaryText:
1946年初夏からスカンジナビア各地でいわゆる「ゴースト・ロケッツ」と呼ばれる飛翔体の目撃が相次いだ。大部分の報告は非専門家によるもので、形状は「尾のある火の玉」や「光沢ある葉巻型」と多様、高度は樹冠付近から16万フィート、速度の記述もまちまちだった。公式調査はスウェーデン防務参謀本部が実施したが資料不足や担当者の欠席など不備があり、参謀本部の発表内容は時期によって変化、政治的配慮があったと分析される。信頼できる目撃例の一つにスウェーデン空軍機パイロットの報告があるが、破片や着弾の直接証拠は確認されていない。報告のうち高高度のものは隕石や花火等と見なされるものが多く、最良の証拠ではV-1型に類する低空飛行ミサイルによる実際の事例は2〜3件、最大でも5〜10件程度にとどまると結論づけられている。ソ連がV-1型の製造・試験能力を有する可能性や、ペーネミュンデ、シュトルプ、バルト諸島周辺での作業の示唆が記されているが、決定的な物的証拠は示されていない。
From late May 1946, numerous reports of so-called "ghost rockets" appeared over Scandinavia. Most sightings were by untrained observers and varied widely: descriptions ranged from "balls of fire with tails" to "shiny cigar-shaped objects," altitudes from tree-top level to 160,000 ft, and speeds from ~65 mph to "lightning fast." The Swedish Defense Staff conducted investigations but displayed procedural shortcomings and issued shifting communiqués, suggesting political considerations. No fragments, impact points, or other direct physical evidence were found; one relatively credible report came from a Swedish Air Force pilot. High-altitude sightings were generally attributable to meteors or fireworks; the best evidence indicates only a small number (2–3, at most 5–10) of real incidents consistent with low-flying V-1–type missiles. The report notes the Soviets' capability and possible testing of V-1–type weapons and mentions Peenemünde, Stolp, and Baltic islands (Oesel, Dago) as implicated areas, but no conclusive physical proof was presented.

This file is a collection of U.S. Government memoranda and correspondence relating to “Project Sign,” a 1948 U.S. Air Force program to investigate reports of high-performance airborne objects. The documents characterize some of these reports as being consistent with “real” objects rather than fabrications or resulting from perceptual errors. The U.S. Air Force cites the reported characteristics of the phenomena, e.g., high speed and maneuverability, as exceeding known performance envelopes of U.S. military aircraft and thereby presenting a potential national security threat, if validated. This potential threat prompted the Air Force to call on the Air Materiel Command (AMC), the Service’s Major Command for logistics and procurement from 1946 to 1961, to gather further evidence to assess the validity of the reports. The Air Force emphasized that there was an “imperative need” for such evidence to enable appropriate countermeasures. The stated urgency of this request reflects the strategic environment of the early Cold War, a period characterized by heightened national defense concerns amid rapid global advancements in aerospace design and development. In framing the call for an investigation, the Air Force noted that sustained public interest and persistent inquiries from the press may eventually require an official statement in response. AMC’s investigation found that observers were generally not mistaken when reporting that they had seen an airborne object, but that their characterizations of those objects as unusual was likely a reflection of the “limits of their personal experience.” It identified “a great many” of the objects reported with a rounded appearance as “weather or upper air scientific balloons of some type.” It also identified several cases in which the reported objects were most likely celestial phenomena, such as Venus. AMC found that a small number of reports lacked a “reasonable everyday explanation,” but that “so far, no physical evidence of the existence of the unidentified sightings has been obtained.” AMC expressly considered whether the phenomena may have been “vehicles from another planet,” but found no evidence supporting such an origin. Ultimately, AMC found that “there is as yet no conclusive proof that unidentified flying objects, other than those which are known to be balloons, are real aircraft.” In light of these findings, AMC recommended that the Department of War should avoid publicly commenting on the subject of “flying discs.” Responding to the Air Force’s anticipated concerns regarding public interest in the subject, AMC recommended that the Department should reply in terms that minimize the investigation’s inconclusive findings, focusing on positive determinations in cases assessed to be weather balloons and celestial phenomena.

1947年12月30日付の指示により「Project SIGN」が設立され、1948年11月の報告は米国内の未確認飛行物体事案についての調査結果と対応方針をまとめている。約180件を調査し、形状別に（a）円盤状、（b）魚雷／葉巻状、（c）球形・気球状、（d）形態を伴わない光の球、に分類した。調査で一部は気象・上層大気用気球や天文現象（例：金星）と確認されたが、多数は確証が得られていない。心理学的要因（幻覚・光学現象・偽情報）の検討、天文物理学者や著名科学者（例：I. Langmuir）への照会を進めている。円盤や葉巻状、光の球については国内起源とは見なされておらず、航空力学的には翼なし機の飛行は理論的に可能だが現行動力では性能に限界があるとの見解が示されている。現時点で物理的証拠（例：残骸）は得られておらず、「これまでに観測された物体を説明できる決定的な証拠はない」という結論と、国防上の必要から起源判定のため調査を継続し、同時に公表すべき情報および対外対応（プレスへの提供か差し控えか）についての見解と勧告を直ちに求める、という要請が含まれる。
The document records that Project SIGN was established following a 30 Dec 1947 directive; the November 1948 correspondence summarizes investigation and policy needs regarding unidentified flying object incidents in the United States. Approximately 180 incidents were studied and categorized by shape: (a) flat circular discs, (b) torpedo/cigar-shaped objects with no visible wings/fins, (c) spherical/balloon-shaped objects, and (d) balls of light with no attached form. Some sightings have been identified as weather/upper-air scientific balloons or as astronomical phenomena (e.g., Venus), but many reports lack definitive confirmation. Psychological factors (hallucination, optical illusion, hoaxes) are being examined in coordination with the Aero‑Medical Laboratory. Consultations with astrophysicists and prominent scientists (including Dr. Irving Langmuir) are ongoing. The report states discs, cigar-shaped objects, and balls of light are not of domestic origin per available information; aerodynamic analysis suggests wingless configurations could sustain flight though current powerplants would limit performance. No physical evidence (such as wreckage) has been obtained, and there is no conclusive proof that unidentified sightings, aside from known balloons, are actual aircraft. The memorandum requests immediate conclusions and recommendations on information to be released to the press and whether to offer or withhold such information until actively sought.

This document is an Intelligence Information Report (IIR), the primary standardized format utilized by the Department of War, military services, and the broader Intelligence Community to disseminate unevaluated intelligence information derived from human sources (HUMINT), open sources, and field collection activities. IIRs are not finished intelligence products; they serve as inputs for subsequent all-source intelligence assessments. This report accompanies the footage contained within DOW-UAP-PR117 through DOW-UAP-PR122. This report documents an observation by the aircrew of a U.S. Special Operations Forces (USSOF) AC-130 Gunship on September 8, 2021, during a nighttime live-fire training exercise over the Gulf of Oman. The aircrew reported first observing two unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) after dropping a water-activated flare. The report describes the UAP as stationary, approximately four feet in diameter, 0-20 feet above the water’s surface. Throughout the training sortie, the aircrew reported observing approximately 25 instances involving similar phenomena via infrared sensor, describing them as “cold orbs.” Aircrew visual estimates of the UAP’s apparent speed range from 250 to 1,300 miles per hour. The report characterizes the UAP’s behavior as “maneuvering aggressively,” “flying in various formations,” and appearing to react to deployments of the aircraft’s onboard weapons systems. The aircrew stated that they were unable to capture video footage of the phenomena because the aircraft’s digital video recorder was not functioning during the incident. All descriptive and estimative language contained in this report reflects the reporter’s subjective interpretation at the time of the event. Such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics.

Date: 8 September 2021. Incident: A USSOF AC-130 gunship conducting nighttime live-fire training over the Gulf of Oman (approximate MGRS location noted) observed approximately 25 instances of unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP). Sequence: While orbiting a water-activated flare, the aircraft's EO/IR sensor detected two ~4-foot-diameter "cold" orbs 0–20 ft above the water, stationary for ~15 seconds. Additional observations: UAPs appeared in IR (white-hot and black-hot) as cold orbs, observed in pairs and three-ship formations, performing coordinated wave-like altitude changes and also flying erratically/aggressively. Estimated speeds: crew used the aircraft TACTOOL and recorded observed maneuvering speeds from ~250 MPH up to ~1300 MPH. No propulsion means were observed. Evidence: videos and a PowerPoint attachment are referenced, but the aircraft DVR inexplicably failed and video data became corrupted. Classification/status: information report, not finally evaluated. Source: direct-access source via official duties; source available for recontact.

This document is a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) Foreign Broadcast Information Service (FBIS) wire report dated November 9, 1963, tracking a local Portuguese-language radio broadcast from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, regarding an alleged crash of a “large metal sphere” containing a deceased occupant in Conde, Bahia, Brazil. This FBIS report is excerpted from the files of Edward C. Welsh, Executive Secretary of the National Aeronautics and Space Council (NASC). NASC was a cabinet-level advisory body within the Executive Office of the President responsible for coordinating U.S. space policy from 1958 to 1973. Handwritten annotations dated November 13, 1963, document a communication between officials at NASC and the U.S. Department of State. The note records a NASC request to a State Department official to query the U.S. Embassy in Rio de Janeiro for local verification of the reporting. This inter-agency request precedes a subsequent diplomatic cable sent by the Embassy the following day, cataloged in this collection under the title “DOS-UAP-D001.”

Interview report of a pilot referred to the FBI. The pilot stated that since October 2023 many pilots have reported seeing white lights in the sky, typically between midnight and 3 AM. The first sighting occurred on a Boston-to-Dublin flight at about 37,000 ft; the lights appeared higher (estimated >50,000 ft), cycled from dim to bright to off (10 seconds to 1 minute), and appeared as 1–4 objects. Some lights were stationary, others moved in straight lines and sometimes changed direction; the pilot did not believe they were Starlink, satellites, meteors, or aircraft landing lights. The pilot has observed them roughly ten times, with durations from 45 minutes to 2 hours, seen in all directions except south, and estimated distances of 200–500 miles. In February 2024 he recorded video on a Samsung Galaxy S22 (approx. 4:36 AM EST, ~150 miles NW of Minneapolis, cockpit video with aircraft at ~0.80 Mach and shown ~40–50 miles NE of Sioux Falls/KFSD). He did not feel unsafe and did not believe the lights were within 100 miles. He also reported a separate June 2002 sighting in Afghanistan near Bagram of a silent equilateral-triangle object (estimated ~500 ft, ~150 kt) that blacked out stars; he found no data explaining that event. He assessed that pilots do not widely discuss these sightings publicly and are not accustomed to talking about them.

In a January 2026 interview, the witness reported observing a UAP on an evening in October 2023 at approximately 10:50 PM from the back porch of his residence in Colorado Springs, accompanied by his wife. The object flew from the northeast toward the southwest at a low altitude (estimated ~300 feet), traveled in a straight line at a consistent elevation, and was observed for about four seconds. It appeared as a triangular shape with rounded edges (unable to determine exact triangle type), possibly dark gray or silver, and exhibited a haze or distortion—described like looking through mist or water ripples—that made it appear semi‑transparent. A silverish‑blue band was visible along the trailing flat edge; the object was silent and produced no perceptible vibration or other effects. The witness stated he is familiar with USAF aircraft and drones and that the observed UAP did not match known aircraft; his wife also observed it and recalled a dark seam around the edge. The record is an FBI FD-302 interview and contains no recommendations or conclusions.

An FBI FD-302 interview report (drafted April 2025, entry May 2025) documents statements from redacted interviewees who reported observing a large black triangular object in June or July 2011 in the evening (around 8–9 PM) while leaving a driveway. Multiple occupants were in the vehicle; one exited and looked up to see a triangle-shaped object flying north. Each corner had a car-sized white light recessed from the corner; the object was low, produced a low humming/pulsing sound, and was observed for approximately 10–15 seconds before passing over a treeline and out of sight. The witnesses were unable to record video in time. One witness estimated an altitude of about 800 feet and dimensions of roughly 200 feet long by 100 feet wide, and recalled a gray/graphite-colored feature in the triangle's center. They did not have a clear memory of the object's thickness or vertical profile, believing they had been underneath it. The report notes the witnesses believed neighbors also observed the object and intended to request written statements or FBI interviews from those neighbors.

A solid black equilateral triangular object emerged from the cloud toward the south/southeast with a diffuse red light on the bottom front point and a red light at each corner. The witness estimated the object could be as large as the parking lot where they stood, about 3–5 stories thick; each light appeared fingernail-sized at arm’s length. Initially it moved south and slightly east at a helicopter-like speed at an estimated altitude of 3,000–5,000 feet, then almost instantaneously accelerated—possibly to Mach 1 or 2—and turned slightly south/southwest. The witness observed wave-like/mirage distortions around the object, heard no noise, saw no visible propulsion, and detected no unusual smell. The object abruptly banked 90 degrees left while veering right, then quickly returned to level flight (a banking motion opposite that of conventional aircraft). The witness lost sight of the object as it passed over a redacted location toward the south; the dark-gray cloud was later gone. About 60 seconds after the sighting the witness called his wife, who reported his voice sounded robotic, suggesting possible electronic interference. The FD-302 notes it contains no FBI conclusions or recommendations.

捜査官の陳述（FD-302）によれば、2026年のある日、約21:00頃、同じ観測区域で熱源として高温に表示される航空物体を観察した。物体は観測地点より西側の尾根2本分ほど離れた位置にあり、地形と距離のため詳細な形状や機体特性は特定できなかったが、熱映像上は南方向へ飛行しているように見え、前夜の目撃方向と整合した。作業中に同地域で稼働していた米陸軍ブラックホークの映像も記録し、比較した結果、当該未確認航空物体はブラックホークの約半分の大きさに見えたと報告する。ただし、この大きさは推定にすぎず、機種、推進方式、固定翼・回転翼・無人機の別は距離と観測限界のため判別できず、物体は地形と距離により観測不能となった。
Per the Special Agent's FD-302 statement, on a date in 2026 at approximately 2100 hours the agent observed a thermally elevated unidentified aerial object in the same western sector and heading as a prior night's sighting. The object appeared about two ridge lines farther west of the previous observation point; terrain and distance prevented identification of specific physical characteristics or exact configuration. The object appeared hot on thermal observation and was flying southbound. The agent recorded video of a U.S. Army Black Hawk in the area as a visual/thermal reference; by comparison the unidentified object appeared approximately half the size of the Black Hawk, an estimate based on appearance, distance, and available footage. The agent could not determine make, model, propulsion type, or whether it was fixed-wing, rotary-wing, or another unmanned system, and the object was eventually lost from observation due to terrain and distance.

This document is an FBI FD-302, a form the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) uses to record interviews. This FD-302 records a 2026 interview with a U.S. person, in which the interviewee describes three incidents potentially involving unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) in the western United States occurring within a 5-hour period in 2026. A second individual who was present at the time also provided an interview, recorded in this collection as “FBI-UAP-D040.” Two FBI digital renderings based upon the observer’s descriptions accompany this document, under the titles FBI-UAP-D038 and FBI-UAP-D039.
この文書は、連邦捜査局 (FBI) がインタビューを記録するために使用するフォームである FBI FD-302 です。このFD-302は、米国人への2026年のインタビューを記録しており、その中でインタビュー対象者は、2026年に5時間以内に米国西部で発生した未確認異常現象（UAP）に関連する可能性のある3つの事件について説明しています。また、当時その場にいた2人目の人物もインタビューを提供しており、このコレクションに「FBI-UAP-D040」として記録されています。この文書には、観察者の説明に基づく 2 つの FBI デジタル レンダリングが、FBI-UAP-D038 および FBI-UAP-D039 というタイトルで添付されています。
初公開
documents.summaryText:
面談者は2026年の夜、同乗者と車で移動中に複数の未確認光を観察したとFBIに供述した。午後8:00～8:30頃、西側の山稜線に沿って移動する2つの鈍い赤色の“ダッシュ状”の光を肉眼で確認し、Night Optical Devices（NODs）越しには円形のオーブ状に見え、NODハローが観察された。約20分後に消失し、その直後に同様の光が真上に現れて約10分後に消えた。午後10～11時の間に東方約600m・上空約500ftに別の光が接近して停止し、さらに別の光が現れて近傍で停止、二番目の光は地上約6ftに見えた。周辺視野で高さを下げて乾いた河床（dry wash）に留まる発光を観察し、光が河床を移動するのを確認したが光源は直接見えなかった。車で位置を移動したが再確認できず、NODのフィルター調整で腕時計表示が携帯電話・車の時計より25分進んでいるのに気付いた（その後24時間放置したところ腕時計は正確に動き続けたが約5分進んだままだったと記載）。面談者はNODsの使用歴25年以上で星や衛星と異なる挙動（方向転換、低高度）を指摘し、排気や音はなく自分の知るUASではないと述べた。熱画像では確認できず、生理的影響や恐怖反応はなく好奇心のみであった。連絡先を提供し追加の接触に応じる旨を伝えた。
The interviewee told the FBI that on a night in 2026 while traveling with a companion they observed multiple unidentified lights. Around 8:00–8:30 PM they saw two dull red, “dash”-shaped lights moving along a western ridgeline; through Night Optical Devices (NODs) these appeared orb-like with a typical NOD halo. After ~20 minutes those lights disappeared and shortly after a similar light appeared overhead for about 10 minutes before disappearing. Between ~10:00–11:00 PM the interviewee observed another light roughly 600 m east and ~500 ft above the vehicle that moved toward them and stopped ~400 m away; a second light then appeared and stopped nearby, the second appearing ~6 ft above ground. In peripheral vision they observed a glow descend and stop in a dry wash ~100 m behind them and saw the glow move through the wash though the source was not directly seen. They drove to a nearer intersection but could not reacquire the lights. While adjusting NOD filters they noted their analog watch showed a time ~25 minutes ahead of their phone and vehicle clocks; the report notes that after 24 hours the watch continued to run accurately but remained ~5 minutes fast. The interviewee, experienced with NODs (25+ years), stated the lights did not behave like stars or satellites, showed direction changes and low altitudes, exhibited no exhaust or audible signature, and were not a UAS familiar to them. Thermal optics did not confirm the objects. No physiological effects or fear were reported; the witness provided contact information and was open to further contact.

Interviewed by an FBI Special Agent via telephone, the subject provided an account of an observation during an area reconnaissance trip on unspecified dates in 2026. After arriving at a gate in heavy rain and waiting for it to subside, they unlocked the gate and drove north. At approximately 2200, after about 25 miles, they noticed a red light at the crest of the mountain range to their west and pulled over. Initially thought to be on the mountain, the light moved east; given a mountain elevation of about 5,000 ft and a cloud base of about 7,000 ft, the subject estimated the light was between 5,000 and 7,000 ft AGL. After roughly 15 minutes, an additional approximately 6–10 lights appeared directly overhead; these lights appeared to 'sync up' with the first and traveled east/southeast. One light descended rapidly (estimated ~1,000 ft) and disappeared; the others continued east/southeast and also disappeared. The lights were described as red and appeared as single points both to the naked eye and through Night Optical Devices, with further observation details truncated in the document. The report contains no FBI recommendations or conclusions.
